researchIntro: These are examples of topics available to undergraduate researchers. Use them as starting points for the questions you want to explore.

research.label: SMALL TRANSFORMERS
research.title: Small Transformers
research.description: We study lightweight models that generate actions and dialogue for game characters. We also use play logs to estimate game difficulty and factors associated with players leaving the game, informing improvements to game balance and player experience.

research.label: DATA-CONSCIOUS GENERATION
research.title: Image generation with limited data
research.description: We investigate high-quality image generation using medium-sized datasets with verified rights and provenance, alongside synthesized data, without relying on unauthorized data collection.

research.label: WORLD MODELS
research.title: World models & interactive AI
research.description: We use approaches such as latent diffusion to predict changes in the environment from video, images, and action sequences. We aim to build world-understanding models and interactive AI for games.

computeText: We use computing resources suited to our research needs and model scale. Our research covers distributed training methods and ways to implement trained models in interactive systems.
projectsIntro: These previous projects connect AI, games, and interaction, offering starting points for new research questions.

projects.name: Kinetics
projects.label: INTERACTION
projects.title: A gamepad controlled by finger tilting
projects.description: A mathematical model for an on-screen gamepad controlled by tilting a finger, exploring new possibilities for touch interaction.

projects.name: Cymotion
projects.label: CHARACTER ANIMATION
projects.title: Characters that respond to their surroundings
projects.description: A next-generation animation system that retrieves and blends motion clips based on context, such as terrain and NPCs, to automatically select suitable character actions.

projects.name: Learned PRNG
projects.label: GENERATIVE MODELS
projects.title: Learning to generate random numbers
projects.description: This project uses existing random-number sequences to train a generator with WGAN-GP, producing sequences that pass the NIST test suite. It explores learned random number generation alongside manually designed algorithms.

projects.name: Sketch2Map
projects.label: CREATIVITY SUPPORT
projects.title: From a hand-drawn sketch to a game map
projects.description: A two-stage conditional GAN system based on pix2pix that turns hand-drawn sketches into game maps. The work is also featured in the book Deep Learning in Gaming and Animations as an application of deep learning to games.

projects.name: Rayauth
projects.label: VISION & AUTHENTICATION
projects.title: Authenticating cards through changing light
projects.description: The model learns spatiotemporal patterns in light produced by holograms and transparent-ink surface structures on cards. Using a smartphone camera, the system distinguishes genuine cards, counterfeit cards, and card images displayed on screens, exploring authentication without embedded chips.
